title: Forecasting scope
text: NYC urban mobility forecasting covers 263 TLC taxi zones, including EWR. The deployed Colab Residual Graph (OD + correlation) ONNX export uses 168 hours of input and directly returns 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24-hour pickup predictions. The demand API is separate from trip pricing. In Trip costs, select pickup and drop-off zones and a departure of now, 1, 3, 6, 12 or 24 hours ahead. Each selection requests time-dependent traffic routing, target-hour weather from Open-Meteo and regulated fare calculation. Rain, snow and fog can produce a labeled travel-time sensitivity range using FHWA speed-reduction studies; this is not a trained NYC fare model. No weather surcharge is added and JFK flat fares do not increase for modeled delay. Each value predicts pickups in one target hour, not a cumulative total. The default current-demand estimate uses an estimated weekly pickup input window and recent Open-Meteo weather with the original training scalers. These are not observed current pickups. The bundled reference is one held-out 2025 week, not full-year seasonal calibration. Every response labels its estimate mode, reference source, model origin and target hour. Accuracy for current conditions is not established. Replay is available only when explicitly selected. A live-observation service needs recent observed demand. The newly supplied notebook reports held-out February/September 2025 benchmark results for all five horizons, using seeded whole-month splits. These historical benchmark scores are not current-demand accuracy and are not cryptographically linked to the deployed ONNX weights. The earlier pre-correction archive covers only 1/3/6 hours. Demand is taxi pickups per zone-hour, not cab availability, fare, passenger wait time or road closure probability.

title: Model comparison: validation-selected GNN and five-horizon saved results
text: The new supplied 2025 notebook contains saved results for 18 models at 1/3/6/12/24 hours. Split seed 42: training Jan, Mar, Apr, Jun, Jul, Aug, Oct, Dec; validation May and Nov; test Feb and Sep. The notebook reports Residual Graph (OD + correlation) as its validation-selected GNN and Seasonal residual (no graph) as its validation-selected baseline. Selected GNN test MAE is 3.301, 3.466, 3.518, 3.593, 3.590 for 1/3/6/12/24 hours; spatial LightGBM is 3.412, 3.877, 3.986, 4.036, 4.030; no-graph GRU is 4.287, 4.432, 4.549, 4.581, 4.529. Lower is better. Selected GNN has lower reported MAE than those two references at all five horizons, but Residual Graph (distance + OD) has lower all-zone test MAE at 12h (3.554) and 24h (3.576). Event and holiday performance can be worse than LightGBM. These are rounded saved outputs, not an independent rerun, a forward-only backtest, or demonstrated current-demand accuracy. Earlier pre-correction LightGBM-leading scores belong to a separate archive with different preprocessing/test months.

title: Graph structure and weights
text: New notebook graph construction uses 50-foot buffered polygon contiguity with three-nearest-neighbor island links; eight-neighbor Gaussian distance; training-month-only OD flow with ten strongest links; and training-month-only positive residual correlation with ten strongest links after removing hour-of-week averages. Saved counts: contiguity 672 edges, mean degree 5.1, 0 isolated; distance 1254 edges, mean 9.5, 0 isolated; OD 2320 edges, mean 17.6, 3 isolated; correlation 2421 edges, mean 18.4, 3 isolated. Edges are modeled relationships, not necessarily drivable roads or causal effects. Earlier counts 2308/2413 for OD/correlation are superseded for this new run and remain only in the old archive.

title: Road construction information
text: NYC DOT Street Closures due to Construction Activities by Block is a planned-work permit feed. Dates and geometry identify reported construction activity, not proof that every lane is currently closed. Only active date intervals are requested. Feed failure means unavailable information, not no closures. Source records may change and may not cover unplanned incidents.

title: MTA subway alerts and timing
text: MTA GTFS-realtime service alerts are filtered by active periods. The Disruptions tab also retrieves official MTA trip updates for a selected station, filters skipped stops and canceled trips, rejects feeds older than five minutes, and shows arrival predictions over the next hour in New York time. Arrival predictions are not guaranteed. Missing data does not establish no service. Train feeds refresh every 30 seconds. Neither arrivals nor alerts establish taxi fares or surge pricing.

title: Disruption impact scenarios
text: The zone disruption score combines geolocated reports within 2.5 km with severity weights and exponential distance decay. It is an uncalibrated heuristic, not a closure prediction probability, observed taxi demand, surge price, verified road routing or trained GNN forecast. Subway alerts without locations remain network notices and do not get assigned fabricated coordinates. Future closure forecasting needs historical incident labels and time-based evaluation.

title: NYC yellow taxi prices
text: TLC standard metered yellow taxi fare: $3 initial, $0.70 per fifth of a mile above 12 mph OR per 60 seconds slow/stopped, $0.50 state surcharge, $1 improvement surcharge, $1 overnight 8pm–6am, $2.50 weekday 4pm–8pm excluding holidays. Manhattan south of 96th: $2.50; applicable Congestion Relief Zone south of and including 60th: $0.75. Add tolls/tips. Trip costs supports the JFK–Manhattan flat fare, JFK and LaGuardia pickup fees, the LaGuardia trip surcharge, and NYC pickups going to Newark Airport. It estimates congestion charges and detected bridge and tunnel tolls from the road route. Uber/Lyft/e-hail prices require provider quotes and cannot be inferred accurately from subway alerts. Trip costs retrieves weather at both zone centers for the selected departure hour and recalculates slow-time sensitivity, time-based charges and routed tolls. Missing weather leaves the traffic-only quote available without fabricated conditions. Forecast weather does not turn the demand GNN into a fare prediction model.

title: Personal knowledge and privacy
text: The private workspace requires a Supabase login and owner-approved membership. Plain text and Markdown documents up to 16,000 characters are stored in a private bucket, chunked and embedded with the configured provider model at 1,024 dimensions (the current Cloudflare setup uses Qwen3-embedding-0.6b). Duplicate content reuses stored vectors. Queries use owner-scoped Postgres semantic cosine and full-text retrieval before ranking. Conversation saving is opt-in, expires 30 days after creation, and supports reopen, export and deletion. Documents expire after 90 days; a protected maintenance job removes expired originals and rows. Source text sent for embeddings and retrieved text sent to Qwen are processed by external providers. Public chat retains bounded conversation context in page memory and sends recent messages for follow-ups, without durable history storage. Structured zone/horizon demand values come directly from the forecast API, with estimate or observation mode attached. Supabase, provider keys and scheduled cleanup require the site owner to configure them; code alone does not provision services.

title: Residual Graph model design and DeepETA inspiration
text: The supplied notebook ResidualGraph architecture declares 168 hours of history, while the base GRU/GCN input window is 12 hours. It corrects a training hour-of-week seasonal profile using recent demand anomalies, daily and weekly anchors, OD/correlation graph mixing, zone/time/horizon embeddings, quantile-bucket weather embeddings and multihead feature-token attention. The notebook adapts ideas from DeepETA for hourly taxi pickup counts; it is not a reproduction of Uber serving or an ETA/fare model. Only saved held-out-month benchmark results are available.
